summary: Fujio Taniguchi works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Nagoya University in 1991 under Musashi Tachikawa and studied under several teachers; he later held posts associated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Fulgence Fresnel was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Pontifical Maronite College in 1826 and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy from around 1826 to 1831.

Fumi Yao specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2011 and became an associate professor there in 2023, while also lecturing at Taisho University.

Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, Yoshiro Tamura, and Kyosho Hayashima, he was a professor at Tokyo (1995–2009) and Nichibunken (~2009–2015).

Fumihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and serves as a special-appointment associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder, later serving as professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).
Fumio Enomoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1982–1984) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1999–2017).

Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He graduated from the University of Tokyo, served as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1953–1965) and Taisho University (~1966–1973), and was president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Matsuda is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an academic committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University, where he served as associate professor (~1993–2002) and professor (~2002–2013).
Fumio Shoji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University, where he later served as an assistant professor (~2014–2018) and associate professor (~2018).
Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University from around 1954 to 1963 and served on its faculty from around 1970 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and later at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing and Shimane International Junior College in the late 1990s.

Futoshi Takehashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as a research assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo works in Tibetology and religious studies. Luo is a PhD student at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026) and holds a post there.

Fyodor Buslaev was a linguist and historian who studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Petrov. He subsequently held posts at Moscow State University beginning in 1846, becoming an adjunkt professor in 1850.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Minaev, Oldenburg, Bühler, and Jacobi, and served as docent and full professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1901 to 1930.

Félicien de Saulcy was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École polytechnique (1826–1828), the military engineering school in Metz (1828–1830), and under Eugène Burnouf.

Félix Lacôte was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet, earning a PhD from the University of Paris. He was deputy at the EPHE (1904–1905) and professor at the University of Lyon (1911).

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from KU Leuven in 1838 before studying under Eugène Burnouf and Christian Lassen. He served as a professor at KU Leuven from 1841 to 1877.
